a refused or failed commit rolls back the lineage/vNNN.md it had already rendered, so a refusal leaves nothing behind at all
a candidate whose higher_is_better differs from the best version's is refused as incomparable rather than ranked — comparing the vectors alone would have silently gotten it backwards

next: S3 — beads memory. `bd init` on `avo init` (which does not exist yet — introduce it, folding in the .avo/.gitignore + .avo/config.json scaffolding avo commit currently does implicitly, and keep it idempotent per invariant 5). `avo mem add "<insight>"` -> `bd remember`; `avo mem` -> `bd prime`. Each committed version gets a bead linked to its parent via `bd dep add` (readLineage already gives you the parent chain: version N-1 is the parent of N); each FAILED attempt gets an insight bead so the agent stops re-trying dead ends across sessions — decideCommit's refusal path already produces exactly the payload to write (reason, comparison deltas, attempt), so hook it there rather than re-deriving. Graceful degradation is the main design constraint: if `bd` is absent, fall back to lineage/memory.jsonl and warn ONCE (invariant 4) — `bd` is an optional dep in avo doctor and most environments will not have it, so the fallback path is the common path and must be tested first. Verify: avo mem add then avo mem | grep the insight; lineage beads show the correct parent chain via bd show; the no-bd fallback has a test. Note the Runner injection pattern (src/score.ts) is how you unit-test the bd calls without bd installed.
